name: Chicken Cafreal
subtitle: chicken marinated green with coriander, chilli and vinegar, then fried dry

ingredients.qty: 800g, legs and thighs, skin off, slashed to the bone
ingredients.note: on the bone only, breast dries out
the stalks carry most of the flavour

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Cafreal is a marinade dish. An hour gives you green chicken with plain meat underneath.
Slash each piece to the bone in two or three places so the paste gets inside.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it cooks evenly.

steps.text: Grind the coriander with stalks, green chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric, vinegar, lemon juice, sugar and 1 tsp salt to a thick green paste. Use no water.
steps.tip: Water dulls the colour and thins the marinade. The vinegar and lemon are enough liquid.

steps.text: Rub the paste hard into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts. Cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy kadhai and lay in the chicken in a single layer, scraping the marinade back into the bowl.
Fry 4 minutes a side over medium-high heat until the surface is seared and patchy brown.
steps.tip: Sear first, marinade later. If you tip everything in together the paste burns before the chicken cooks.

steps.text: Add the reserved marinade and 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook on low for 20 minutes, turning the pieces twice.
Meanwhile fry the quartered potatoes in a separate pan until gold and cooked through, about 12 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat and cook 5-6 minutes more until the sauce has reduced to a thick coating that clings to the chicken.
steps.tip: Cafreal is a dry dish. If there is a pool of gravy in the pan, keep going.

steps.text: Check with a knife at the thickest part of the thigh. The juices should run clear. Squeeze over lemon and serve with the potatoes and pav.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a covered pan with 2 tbsp water over low heat; the microwave makes it stringy. The marinade freezes well for 2 months.
